description: This topic explains the meaning, purposes, types and media of advertising together with sales promotion methods and the merits, demerits and ethics of advertising.

mcq.questionText: What is the main meaning of advertising in commerce?

options.text: A way of paying tax to the government
A paid form of communication used to inform and persuade people about goods or services
A method of storing goods in a warehouse
A type of insurance against business loss

mcq.explanation: Advertising is a paid, non-personal form of communication that informs and persuades buyers about a product, service or idea.

mcq.questionText: Which type of advertising mainly gives facts such as price, location and features of a product?
mcq.explanation: Informative advertising concentrates on giving facts and useful information so that customers can know about a product.

mcq.questionText: An advertisement that tries to make a firm's product look better than that of a rival firm is called:
mcq.explanation: Competitive advertising compares a product with that of competitors to win a larger share of the market.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an advertising medium?
mcq.explanation: A radio station is a medium through which advertising messages are carried to the audience.

mcq.questionText: Which advertising medium is best for reaching many people who cannot read or write?
mcq.explanation: Radio uses sound and spoken words, so it reaches illiterate people who cannot read printed media.

mcq.questionText: Giving a buyer a reduction in price for buying in large quantities is a sales promotion method known as:
mcq.explanation: A discount is a reduction in the selling price offered to encourage buying or prompt payment.

mcq.questionText: A small free portion of a product given to customers to try is called a:
mcq.explanation: A free sample lets customers test a product before deciding to buy it.

mcq.questionText: A voucher that allows a customer to buy goods at a reduced price is called a:
mcq.explanation: A coupon is a printed voucher that gives the holder a price reduction or a special offer on a product.

mcq.questionText: Repairing, servicing or replacing a product after it has been sold is an example of:
mcq.explanation: After-sales service includes help, repairs and servicing given to the buyer after a purchase to keep them satisfied.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a demerit (disadvantage) of advertising?

options.text: It increases the cost of goods to the consumer
It informs customers about new products
It widens the market for producers

mcq.explanation: Advertising costs are usually added to the price of goods, making them more expensive for consumers.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a merit (advantage) of advertising to the consumer?

options.text: It can mislead buyers with false claims
It informs consumers about available goods and prices
It increases the price of goods

mcq.explanation: Advertising informs consumers about the existence, qualities and prices of goods, helping them make choices.

mcq.questionText: An advertisement that gives false or exaggerated information about a product is described as:
mcq.explanation: Misleading advertising deceives the buyer with untrue or exaggerated claims about a product.

mcq.questionText: Which type of advertising aims mainly at convincing customers to buy by appealing to their emotions and desires?
mcq.explanation: Persuasive advertising tries to influence and convince customers to buy rather than merely giving facts.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the main purpose of advertising for a producer?

options.text: To reduce the quality of goods
To increase sales and widen the market

mcq.explanation: A key purpose of advertising is to boost demand, increase sales and reach a wider market for the producer.

mcq.questionText: Which advertising medium would be MOST suitable for a businessperson who wants to demonstrate how a product is used through moving pictures and sound?
mcq.explanation: Television combines sight, sound and motion, so it can effectively demonstrate how a product works.

fib.questionText: Advertising is a _____ form of communication, meaning the advertiser must pay for it.
fib.explanation: Unlike publicity, advertising is paid for by the advertiser.

fib.questionText: The type of advertising that simply provides facts about a product is called _____ advertising.
fib.explanation: Informative advertising gives information such as price and features.

fib.questionText: The type of advertising that compares a product with rivals to gain more customers is called _____ advertising.
fib.explanation: Competitive advertising is used to outdo competing products.

fib.questionText: A reduction in the price of goods given to encourage buying is called a _____.
fib.explanation: Discounts are a common sales promotion tool.

fib.questionText: A small free portion of a product given to customers to try is called a free _____.
fib.explanation: Free samples encourage customers to test and then buy a product.

fib.questionText: A printed voucher that gives a customer a price reduction is known as a _____.
fib.explanation: Coupons attract buyers by offering them a discount on a product.

fib.questionText: Repairs and servicing offered to a buyer after a purchase are known as _____ service.
fib.explanation: After-sales service keeps customers satisfied and loyal.

fib.questionText: Advertising that gives false or exaggerated claims about a product is described as _____ advertising.
fib.explanation: Misleading advertising deceives buyers and is considered unethical.

fib.questionText: A general term for activities other than advertising used to boost sales, such as discounts and free gifts, is sales _____.
fib.explanation: Sales promotion includes short-term incentives to encourage buying.

fib.questionText: The channel through which an advertising message reaches the audience, such as radio or television, is called the advertising _____.
fib.explanation: An advertising medium carries the message from the advertiser to the audience.

tf.questionText: Advertising is always free and never paid for by the advertiser.
tf.explanation: Advertising is a paid form of communication, unlike free publicity.

tf.questionText: Informative advertising mainly gives facts and information about a product.
tf.explanation: It focuses on details such as price, features and where to buy.

tf.questionText: Persuasive advertising tries to convince customers to buy a product.
tf.explanation: Persuasive advertising appeals to emotions and desires to influence buyers.

tf.questionText: A free sample is a method of sales promotion.
tf.explanation: Free samples encourage customers to try and then buy products.

tf.questionText: A coupon is a document that proves payment has been received.
tf.explanation: A coupon is a voucher giving a price reduction; a receipt proves payment.

tf.questionText: After-sales service is given to the buyer before a product is bought.
tf.explanation: After-sales service is provided after the purchase, for example repairs and servicing.

tf.questionText: One demerit of advertising is that its cost may be added to the price of goods.
tf.explanation: Advertising expenses are often passed on to consumers, raising prices.

tf.questionText: Radio is a useful advertising medium for reaching people who cannot read.
tf.explanation: Radio relies on sound, so it reaches illiterate audiences.

tf.questionText: Misleading advertising is honest and gives only true information.
tf.explanation: Misleading advertising gives false or exaggerated claims and is dishonest.

tf.questionText: Truthful advertising helps to build trust and a good reputation for a business.
tf.explanation: Honest advertising builds customer confidence and long-term goodwill.

summary.correctAnswer: A paid form of communication used to inform and persuade people about goods or services.
summary.explanation: It aims to increase awareness and sales.

summary.correctAnswer: To inform, persuade and remind customers in order to increase sales and widen the market.
summary.explanation: It supports demand for products and services.

summary.correctAnswer: Advertising that mainly gives facts and information about a product.
summary.explanation: Example: stating price, features and location.

summary.correctAnswer: Advertising that aims to convince and influence customers to buy.
summary.explanation: It appeals to emotions and desires.

summary.correctAnswer: Advertising that compares a product with rivals to win more customers.
summary.explanation: Used to gain a larger market share.

summary.correctAnswer: Channels that carry advertising messages, such as radio, television, newspapers and posters.
summary.explanation: Each medium reaches a different audience.

summary.correctAnswer: Short-term incentives such as discounts, free samples, coupons and after-sales service.
It informs consumers and widens the market, increasing sales for producers.
summary.explanation: It also creates employment in the advertising industry.

summary.correctAnswer: It can increase the price of goods and may sometimes mislead buyers.
summary.explanation: Costs are passed on to consumers.

summary.correctAnswer: Truthful advertising gives honest information while misleading advertising gives false or exaggerated claims.
summary.explanation: Honest advertising builds trust; misleading advertising is unethical.

hoq.questionText: A new soft-drink company with a small budget wants many people in both towns and rural villages, including those who cannot read, to learn how to prepare and enjoy its drink. Which combination of media and promotion would be MOST effective?

options.text: Only printed newspapers with long written instructions
Radio advertising together with free samples given out in markets
Posters written in small print placed inside offices

hoq.explanation: Radio reaches both literate and illiterate audiences cheaply, while free samples let people try the drink, making this the most effective low-budget combination.

hoq.questionText: A trader advertises that her soap 'cures all skin diseases within one day,' although this is not true, and sales rise sharply at first. What is the MOST likely long-term result of this approach?

options.text: Customers will trust the business even more over time
Customers will lose trust once the claim proves false, harming the business reputation
The soap will automatically improve in quality
Competitors will be forced to lower their prices permanently

hoq.explanation: This is misleading advertising; when customers discover the false claim they lose trust, which damages the trader's reputation and future sales.

hoq.questionText: Two shops sell the same brand of phone at the same price, but one shop offers free repair and servicing for one year after purchase. Why might more customers choose the second shop even though prices are equal?

options.text: Because it offers after-sales service, which adds value and confidence to the purchase
Because after-sales service makes the phone cheaper to produce
Because after-sales service is a form of misleading advertising
Because after-sales service reduces the quality of the phone

hoq.explanation: After-sales service gives buyers extra value and confidence, so customers prefer the shop offering it even when prices are the same.
